title: Project authority and roadmap recovery

authority.purpose: Record the temporary recovery sequence required to finish roadmap migration, reconcile language authority, simplify orchestration, and resume ordinary roadmap execution.

goals: Finish the machine-readable roadmap migration so current and future work can be selected deterministically.
Reconcile historical language-design initiatives so only the current Core-owned language authority governs future implementation.
Remove stale blocking authority from superseded planning gates without deleting useful historical evidence.
Restore thin orchestration in which workflow state, roadmap state, and the previous validated handoff can be consumed without broad repository reinterpretation.
Complete the end-to-end projection of the self-described Core language only after authority recovery is complete.

audit.summary: roadmap/v1 now represents all 26 current milestones as authoritative JSON milestones and migration.pending_milestones is empty.
M10.1 through M10.3 remain useful compatibility, migration, and conformance evidence but are no longer the permanent semantic language authority after the Core authority transition.
The accepted Core Language Authority Gate and subsequent binding self-description correction establish direct Core/Core-authored modules as the permanent semantic authority.
M16.5 remains useful design and evaluation evidence, but its historical blocking rules must not override later accepted Core authority decisions.

packages.title: Complete roadmap/v1 migration
packages.goal: Make the current project roadmap deterministically queryable without requiring the orchestrator to reinterpret TODO/backlog prose.
work: Extend roadmap/v1 to cover all current milestone authorities, at minimum M10.5 through M21 including M16.5.
Preserve existing milestone and work-package IDs, status, order, priority, dependencies, evidence, references, and terminal dispositions conservatively.
Add schema support for explicit authority or supersession relationships where needed.
Keep blocked state derived from status plus dependency graph.
Update tools/roadmap.py and tests only where required to query the completed graph deterministically.
Bind TODO/backlog status projections to JSON authority with deterministic drift checks.
acceptance_criteria: Every active milestone is represented in roadmap/v1 or intentionally excluded with an explicit terminal disposition.
python3 tools/roadmap.py validate succeeds on the complete current graph.
python3 tools/roadmap.py next identifies the actual dependency-ready current work including the active M10.5 sequence.
Unknown IDs, cycles, duplicate IDs or order, invalid supersession, and Markdown/JSON status drift fail deterministically.
No project semantics, parser behavior, runtime behavior, or compiler behavior changes in this package.

packages.title: Reconcile the language-authority chain
packages.goal: Make the accepted language authority unambiguous across roadmap, specification, grammar, and historical design gates.
authority_chain: Revision-4 M10.1/M10.2/M10.3 artifacts are historical compatibility, migration, and conformance evidence.
The accepted Core Language Authority Gate and binding self-description correction govern current semantic authority.
M16.5 remains historical design and evaluation evidence and does not independently block a later accepted Core authority decision.
Generated projections and meta-IR remain derived and non-authoritative.
work: Record explicit supersedes or superseded_by relationships in the machine-readable roadmap or authority model.
Correct stale durable documentation claims that still present revision-4 spec/language-surface-v1.json as current semantic authority.
Preserve revision-4 material for compatibility and regression evidence.
Make M16.5 distinguish historical design gates from current blocking authority.
acceptance_criteria: No durable project document claims that revision 4 and direct Core are simultaneous permanent semantic authorities.
Current authority can be determined without interpreting chronological SpecialTask history.
Historical compatibility and evaluation evidence remains available and referenced.
Repository validation detects contradictory authority markers where practical.

packages.title: Add deterministic roadmap context projection for agents
packages.goal: Give orchestrators and executors a compact read-only view of relevant project roadmap state analogous to existing Channel workflow projections.
work: Extend tools/roadmap.py or add a small read-only wrapper with stable JSON output for one current item or initiative.
Include direct dependencies, transitive blockers, next dependency-ready candidates, authority and supersession information, remaining acceptance criteria, and evidence/reference paths.
Do not make strategic language decisions inside the tool; decisions must already exist in authoritative project data.
Keep output deterministic, bounded, offline, and suitable for LLM consumption.
acceptance_criteria: An orchestrator can obtain current roadmap context without rereading all of TODO/backlog.
The projection never invents state not present in authoritative roadmap data.
Stable tests cover ready, blocked, superseded, terminal, and invalid graph cases.

packages.title: Restore thin orchestration semantics
packages.goal: Return the orchestrator to routing and bounded decision-making rather than broad project-state reconstruction.
normal_inputs: current Channel orchestrator-context and admission state
current roadmap context and next dependency-ready work
previous validated result and its next_task when present
explicit active SpecialTask or initiative only when it intentionally overrides ordinary roadmap sequencing
rules: Prefer an explicit valid next_task from the previous result when it remains consistent with current authoritative project state.
Use roadmap dependency order as the ordinary fallback.
Escalate to broad architecture or planning analysis only when the handoff is absent, blocked, contradictory, or an active SpecialTask intentionally changes direction.
A newer accepted initiative must explicitly supersede conflicting older gates rather than silently coexist with them.
acceptance_criteria: Routine completed work advances without a full repository-wide planning pass.
SpecialTask-driven direction changes leave durable authority or supersession state in the project.
Workflow safety checks remain deterministic and separate from semantic project decisions.

packages.title: Complete the self-described Core public-language rollout
packages.goal: Finish the already accepted Core architecture end-to-end instead of starting another competing language-design initiative.
work: Treat the current self-described Core and Bootstrap boundary as the starting authority.
Reconcile normative grammar documentation with that authority.
Migrate positive examples, reference applications, and fixtures to the intended current language surface or explicitly classify them as compatibility, rejection, or historical evidence.
Align parser, AST, IR, resolver, type checking, diagnostics, formatter, and IDE surfaces only as required by the accepted Core language contract.
Add deterministic drift and conformance checks between Core authority, grammar projection, examples, and implementation behavior.
Preserve revision-4 compatibility paths only where explicitly required.
acceptance_criteria: docs/06-grammar.md is a projection of the current Core-owned language rather than an independent revision-4 authority.
Representative Core declaration kinds and examples are accepted end-to-end by the intended implementation path.
Positive examples no longer teach syntax that conflicts with current Core authority.
Historical or compatibility syntax is explicitly classified and tested as such.
No unresolved permanent dual-authority language model remains.

packages.title: Resume ordinary milestone execution
packages.goal: Return to normal roadmap-driven product development.
work: Recompute the next dependency-ready work from the complete machine-readable roadmap.
Resume M10.5 and later milestones only against the reconciled language authority.
Continue focused implementation, independent validation where applicable, unchanged-head integration, and deterministic CI.
acceptance_criteria: Project progression is determined by machine-readable roadmap state plus explicit active initiatives, not historical conversation or SpecialTask reconstruction.
Future SpecialTasks either complete their rollout or leave an explicit supersession or follow-up package in the roadmap before they are considered closed.

invariants: Do not create another independent roadmap or language authority.
Do not discard useful historical evidence merely because its authority role changed.
Do not let a planning or evaluation gate silently override a later accepted architecture decision.
Every direction-changing initiative must explicitly record what it supersedes.
Every partially migrated authority must have an explicit remaining migration package.
Prefer deterministic read-only tooling over repeated LLM reconstruction of repository state.
New workflow rules should replace obsolete complexity rather than merely accumulate beside it.
